ONE WINDOW. SEVERAL CHOICES.

These terms can work together.

They are not mutually exclusive glass types. A double-glazed unit can combine toughened glass and a Low-E coating; laminated, tinted or obscure glass can also be part of a suitable unit.

CHOOSE BY PERFORMANCE

Three priorities.
Seven glass choices.

Start with the job you need your glass to do. These groups can combine in one window; they are not quality tiers. Typical uses do not confirm project suitability or current FABINT stock.

01 Light & privacy ↓ 02 Thermal comfort ↓ 03 Safety & protection ↓

01 / DAYLIGHT, VIEWS & APPEARANCE

Light & privacy

Choose how much you see, how much light enters and how the glass looks. Tint and obscurity do not replace the required safety treatment.

01

BASE GLASS

Clear float

Clear, flat glass for natural light and unobstructed views. It is also the starting material for many processed glass products.

Typical use
General glazing where suitable, or a base for toughened, laminated and coated glass.
Know the limit
Ordinary annealed float is not safety glass. Clear appearance does not tell you its safety or thermal performance.
Source: Viridian · VFloat ↗
02

COLOUR & SOLAR CONTROL

Tinted

Colour within the glass can reduce glare and incoming solar heat, while changing the amount and colour of daylight.

Typical use
Glare-prone glazing where the daylight and colour trade-offs suit the design.
Know the limit
Tint is not a substitute for insulation or safety treatment. Absorbed heat can require a thermal-stress assessment.
Source: Viridian · clear and toned glass ↗
03

PRIVACY FINISH

Frosted / obscure

An etched surface, pattern or translucent interlayer softens views while still admitting light.

Typical use
Privacy-focused windows and partitions where clear views are less important than daylight.
Know the limit
Obscurity varies by product. It does not automatically provide complete privacy or safety-glass performance.
Source: Viridian · privacy products ↗Viridian · obscurity FAQ ↗

02 / HEAT TRANSFER & INSULATION

Thermal comfort

Manage heat moving through your window. The right combination depends on climate, orientation, frame and installation—not a coating or pane count alone.

04

PERFORMANCE COATING

Low-E

A low-emissivity coating reduces heat transfer through the glass. Different coatings balance daylight and solar control differently.

Typical use
Windows where thermal comfort is a priority, with the coating selected for the climate and project.
Know the limit
Low-E does not mean double glazing. Some hard-coat products work in single glazing; soft-coat products typically need protection inside an insulated unit.
Source: Australian Glass Group · Low-E FAQ ↗
05

ASSEMBLED UNIT

Double glazing / IGU

Two panes separated by a sealed cavity improve insulation compared with ordinary single glazing. IGU means insulated glass unit.

Typical use
Energy-performance-focused windows and doors. The panes, cavity and coating are selected together.
Know the limit
Double glazing alone does not mean Low-E or safety glass. Compare the complete window, including its frame, seals and installation.
Source: Viridian · glass choices explained ↗

03 / STRENGTH & BREAKAGE BEHAVIOUR

Safety & protection

Choose glass for how it handles impact and behaves if broken. The required glass and supporting system must be specified for the location and use.

06

SAFETY TREATMENT

Toughened

Heat-treated for greater strength and impact resistance. If broken, it fragments into small pieces rather than large sharp shards.

Typical use
Correctly specified windows, doors, shower screens and splashbacks.
Know the limit
It is not unbreakable. A broken monolithic pane can fall out of its opening; toughening alone does not retain the fragments.
Source: Viridian · VTough ↗National Glass · breakage guide (PDF) ↗
07

BONDED CONSTRUCTION

Laminated

Two or more glass sheets bonded to an interlayer that helps hold fragments together if the glass breaks.

Typical use
Suitable window and door systems where fragment retention matters. Acoustic and security versions need their own specification.
Know the limit
Laminated glass alone does not guarantee fall protection. Post-breakage performance depends on the glass, interlayer and support system.
Source: Viridian · VLam ↗National Glass · design notes (PDF) ↗

COMBINE, THEN CUSTOMISE

Custom is a choice.
Not a performance class.

Size, tint and finish choices can apply across these groups, subject to supplier confirmation and the required specification. A privacy finish, safety treatment and thermal coating can work together in a suitable window.

Thermal performance is not a blanket sustainability claim. Environmental benefits need product-specific evidence, including the complete window and its use.

BEFORE YOU CHOOSE

Compare the specification.
Then the price.

  • Coating, cavity and safety treatment
  • Supplier evidence for the complete product
  • Warranty, inclusions and delivered cost in AUD
